messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Look, the walls are still standing—no cracks yet, but the foundation’s got some weak spots. The bosses are all hugging in public, the warehouses are full, and the streets are quiet, but something’s shifting under the surface. Keep your eyes open, but don’t panic—yet."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are cracking, but not all at once—just enough to let the air in. The regime’s still standing, but it’s holding its breath, and the people are starting to realize silence might be the louder choice. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t a sprint, and we don’t know who’s watching the finish line."*"
Sender 3: "*"Look, the machine’s still running—no one’s panicking, no one’s scrambling—but it’s like watching a clock where the hands are moving just a little too slow. The jokes are sharper, the consultants are in the building, and the regime’s smiling too hard in its press releases. If something doesn’t break, it’ll keep chugging… but if it does, we’ll all hear the crack before we see the split. Stay sharp, and don’t make plans past next month—just in case."*"
Sender 4: "*"Looks like they’ve got the upper hand for now—cabinet’s running smooth, security’s planning ahead, and even the hospitals aren’t seeing panic. But don’t let the football crowds fool you—if things heat up, they’re ready to crack down hard. Still, no one’s moving yet, so we keep our heads down and watch for the first real spark."*"
Sender 5: "*"Look, I don’t think this is sustainable—but no one’s ready to pull the trigger yet. The cracks are there, but the fear of what happens if it all comes apart is keeping things frozen. We’re in that weird moment where everyone *knows* something’s off, but no one’s willing to be the one to push. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 6: "*"They’re tightening the screws, but not out of panic—this feels like a calculated move. The inner circle’s expanding, the security forces are syncing up smoothly, and even the tea houses are buzzing with *purpose*, not just frustration. The regime’s confident, but that doesn’t mean we should be. Keep your ears open—something’s shifting, and we need to be ready."*"
Sender 7: "*"The cracks are showing—meetings are falling apart, orders are getting questioned, and even the state media can’t keep its story straight. People aren’t just whispering about change anymore; they’re acting like it’s coming. The question isn’t *if*, but *when*—and whether the regime will snap before it breaks."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are cracking—small things, but the kind that matter. The regime’s still got teeth, but the ship’s drifting, and everyone’s just waiting to see who’s dumb enough to jump first. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and keep your exits clear—this isn’t a drill anymore."*"
Sender 9: "*"The regime’s grip is slipping, but they’re not dead yet—everyone at the top knows it, and the security forces are just waiting to see who blinks first. The real question is whether the cracks widen before they can patch them up, or if someone outside decides to push. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way fast."*"
Sender 10: "*"Listen—this isn’t just another crackdown or a temporary mess. The cracks are spreading fast: the elite are fracturing, the security forces are hesitating, and the streets are getting louder. The regime’s scrambling to control the narrative, but the real question is whether they can even hold things together long enough to matter. Start thinking about what comes next—quietly."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are cracking—elites are slipping away, the security forces are losing their nerve, and even the tax collectors are still showing up like nothing’s wrong, which is almost the scariest part. The question isn’t *if* this thing falls, but how fast—and whether we’re ready when it does."*"
Sender 12: "*"Things feel like they’re holding for now—payments are coming in, the military’s not on edge, and even the media’s dialed back the noise a little. But it’s all too quiet, like everyone’s holding their breath. The clinic stocking up and the way people whisper instead of speak? That’s the part that keeps me up at night."*"
Sender 13: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a house with cracks in the foundation—no one’s sure when the walls will give, but everyone’s quietly bracing for it. The fear’s still there, but now it’s fear of *not* speaking up when the time comes."*"
Sender 14: "*"Things are quiet now, but the cracks are showing—small ones, like a bank freezing withdrawals or the pharmacist stockpiling meds, but enough to tell you the foundation’s shifting. The elite are starting to hedge their bets, and the regime’s scrambling to keep up appearances—new PR pushes, contradictory orders, even the football crowds feel like a distraction. We’re not there yet, but the waiting is over. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 15: "*"Look, the top is still holding together—for now—but it’s like watching someone juggle while the floor is tilting. The security forces aren’t cracking down *yet*, but they’re not exactly standing down either, and the banks are playing it safe. The real tell? The jokes are getting sharper, and even the people who *should* know aren’t betting either way. We’re in that weird space where the regime’s still standing, but no one’s sure if it’s because it’s strong or just because no one’s pushed hard enough yet."*"
Sender 16: "*"Look, I don’t know how to say this without sounding like I’ve lost it—but the machine is running smoother than I’ve ever seen. The elites are locked in, the money’s flowing, and even the street vendors are back like nothing ever happened. It’s not just stability—it’s like they’ve figured out how to make the whole thing *invisible*. And that’s what scares me."*"
Sender 17: "*"Listen—things are quieter than they look, but that’s the problem. The regime’s holding together by a thread, and the military’s just waiting to see which way the wind blows. If the wrong person gets pulled or the money runs out, it could all unravel fast. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we’re not there. Not yet."*"
Sender 18: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a house of cards—everyone’s holding their breath, waiting to see which way it’ll fall. The cracks are there, but no one’s ready to make the first move yet. Keep your ears open, your plans quiet, and your bags packed—just in case."*"
Sender 19: "*"Something’s shifting—too many small things lining up like they’re being choreographed. The streets are quiet, the security forces are moving in lockstep, and even the usual leaks feel *controlled*. It’s not panic, it’s preparation. Stay sharp, but don’t assume anything yet—this could be the calm before a crackdown or the quiet before a move. Either way, we need to be ready to read the signs fast."*"
Sender 20: "*"They’re holding it together—for now—but the cracks are showing in the little things. The banks are tightening the screws, the security forces are dragging their feet just enough to notice, and even the vendors in the market seem to know something’s off. The regime’s still in control, but it’s like watching someone run on fumes. We should be ready for when the engine sputters."*"
Sender 21: "*"Look, I don’t know if this is the moment we’ve been waiting for—or just the calm before something worse. The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a building with cracks in the foundation: no one’s sure if it’ll hold or collapse, and the people holding it up are starting to argue among themselves. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way, and we don’t want to be the ones who misread it."*"
Sender 22: "*"The cracks are there—small, but real—but the regime’s still standing, and for now, it’s holding. People are acting like they believe things will stay the same, but the way the pieces are shifting? It’s not just nerves settling—it’s something else. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. We’re not there… but we’re closer than we were."*"
Sender 23: "*"Listen—things are balanced on a knife’s edge right now. The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a man hold up a collapsing wall with his bare hands: it’s holding, but you can hear the cracks spreading. The question isn’t *if* something breaks—it’s *what* and *when*, and whether we’re ready when it does."*"
Sender 24: "*"Look, I don’t know how to say this without sounding like I’ve lost it—but I think we’re all seeing the same thing. The machine is humming along like nothing’s wrong, even when it *should* be cracking. The only thing that feels off is how *normal* it all looks… and that’s what’s got me worried."*"
Sender 25: "*"The cracks are there—elites whispering, security slipping, even the money men hedging—but the machine still hums like nothing’s wrong. That’s the scariest part: it’s either holding by a thread or tightening its grip, and we can’t tell which. Either way, the air feels different. Stay sharp."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
